summary.one_liner: A Claude Code and claude.ai plugin that measures token and context costs, adds Haiku subagents for cheap reading and test runs, and runs locally with no telemetry.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes a set of skills for claude.ai chat, desktop and Cowork (fresh-start handoffs, doc-digest summaries, project-context instructions, token-check sizing, sharpen-prompt rewrites). In Claude Code it adds two Haiku 5.5 subagents: scout for read-only project exploration and runner for tests, builds and linters, so only their short answers enter the main context. A /cco command provides a session board, transcript audit, budget and cache warnings, task state that survives /compact, file packing by line range, and git-aware context. Read dedup skips re-reads of unchanged files in the same context. Data is stored locally in ~/.claude-context-optimizer/, and exports can be Markdown or an offline HTML page.
use_cases: reduce token spend in long Claude Code sessions
audit where Claude API costs went in past sessions
hand off a long chat to a new conversation
summarize a long document for ongoing work
run tests or builds through a cheaper model
track budget and prompt cache warnings in Claude Code
how_to_run: git clone the repo and run: claude --plugin-dir ~/claude-context-optimizer (for development)
Requires Node.js 18 or later and a POSIX shell for hooks (Git Bash or WSL on Windows)
npm test runs the test suite
notable: Haiku subagents (scout, runner) keep bulk reading out of the expensive model's context
Read dedup skips unchanged re-reads and substitutes a file landmark map
Local-only: no telemetry, no network calls from plugin code, zero config by default
Covers claude.ai and Cowork skills as well as Claude Code hooks and commands
Audit of own transcripts with totals only, and an offline HTML export
caveats: Hooks need Node.js and a POSIX shell; Windows requires Git Bash or WSL
Skills-only use works on claude.ai and Cowork, but the full feature set is Claude Code only
README says the design is still somewhat exploratory (per listing description)
